notes:
Need to search first.Let me do fewer searches at once.I couldn't find anything for Jeremiah 12, so I have no notes to give you.

The research failed early. My first attempt to open the pages directly (Enduring Word, Precept Austin, BibleHub's Ellicott, Gill and Pulpit commentaries, and NET Bible notes) was refused, because the tool only opens addresses that have first come up in a search. My next step was to run about ten searches at once, and that went over the tool's usage limit. Every later call was blocked as well. Not one page loaded, so I have nothing on any verse, any Protestant tradition, modern scholarship, Catholic or Orthodox readings, or popular modern teaching.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never to fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written any verse notes from memory, because they would have no sources and no URLs.

**To finish this in a new session, I'd:**
1. Run a few searches at a time instead of many at once, to stay under the limit. Some useful ones would be "Jeremiah 12 enduringword", "Jeremiah 12 Ellicott biblehub", "Jeremiah 12 Gill", "Jeremiah 12 Pulpit commentary", "preceptaustin Jeremiah 12" and "netbible Jeremiah 12".
2. Open the verse-by-verse pages those searches turn up and pull out notes for each verse.
3. Search specific topics separately, such as the prosperity of the wicked (vv. 1–4), "running with horses" (v. 5), and the promise to the neighbouring nations (vv. 14–17). I'd also try the tradition sites like wesley.nnu.edu, gty.org, desiringgod.org, newadvent.org and others.
4. Write the notes verse by verse ("v. 1: …"), with a URL after every point and verses left out where nothing turns up.

If you send the request again, I'll start with step 1.
